shortDescription: Nordic forward power prices rose on Friday, snapping a three-day losing streak, supported by gains in European energy markets, but were headed for a weekly decline on improving water reserves in the hydropower-dependent region.

children: Nordic forward power prices rose on Friday, snapping a three-day losing streak, supported by gains in European energy markets, but were headed for a weekly decline on improving water reserves in the hydropower-dependent region.
Nordic front-quarter baseload power contract (NSBLQc1) rose€2.82, or 2.6%, to €111.60 per megawatt hour (MWh) at 1056 GMT
Nordic front-year (NSBLYc1) gained €1.58, or 2.4%, to €67.40 per MWh.

Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices firmed, after three days of decline, on support from disruptions to liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipping, Norwegian maintenance and low European storage levels.
"Firmer gas supporting the energy complex and risks towards drier conditions could be driving the sentiment ahead of the weekend," said analysts at Mind Energy in a note.
German power prices traded higher for next week as low renewable output is expected and dry conditions continue to reduce output at French nuclear power plants.
Germany's year-ahead power (TRDEBYc1), Europe's benchmark contract, rose €3.62, or 2.8%, to €131.45 per MWh.

Meanwhile, Nordic water reserves available 15 days ahead (PCAEC00) were seen at 9.86 terawatt hours (TWh) below normal, compared with 10.40 TWh below normal on Thursday.

On the weather front, "next week will be less active and sunnier in the south while the north will remain unsettled with near normal rain. Temperatures will be near or slightly above normal. The week after next week could be generally dry and quite warm with slightly above-normal temperatures," said LSEG meteorologist Georg Muller.
Improving water reserves weigh on Nordic power prices, while forecasts for drier weather provided some support.
